source.authors: Robert Sigl, Sebastian Steibl, Christian Laforsch
source.title: The role of vision for navigation in the crown-of-thorns seastar, Acanthaster planci

method: light microscopy of dissected compound eyes of arm tips; the Results give the average angle between the optical axes of neighbouring ommatidia
conditions: Wild adults collected around Moorea, French Polynesia, and kept without food in plastic bins with running seawater for 2-4 weeks before use (Methods, Experimental animals and area). Nine adults supplied one arm tip each; the Methods say one small (about 15 cm diameter) and four large (30-50 cm diameter) dissected eyes were used for the visual-field approximation, and the paper does not restate in the Results sentence how many eyes the average rests on. 11.2 ± 5.9 deg (± not defined as SD or SE); the following Results sentence says the angle varies across the eye, from dense areas to dispersed areas, so 11.2 deg is an eye-wide average, not a local value. Large individuals had 192-268 ommatidia per eye.
where: Results, Spatial resolution and visual field of the compound eye
quote: The average distance of the optical axes of neighbouring ommatidia is 11.2 ± 5.9°.
note: New-to-main value for this species; interommatidial_deg is a trait key already on main. Whole Results sentence (14 words), read intact in a second pass with its neighbours (the sentence before and after it were seen only in truncated form, which does not affect this sentence). Value is the sentence's mean; the ± term is kept in conditions. source.authors: Robert Sigl, Sebastian Steibl, Christian Laforsch
source.title: The role of vision for navigation in the crown-of-thorns seastar, Acanthaster planci

method: semi-thin sections of embedded eyes; acceptance angle of single ommatidia derived from the sectioned ommatidial structure (the Results sentence gives the minimum and maximum)
conditions: Wild adults collected around Moorea, French Polynesia, and kept without food in plastic bins with running seawater for 2-4 weeks before use (Methods, Experimental animals and area). Four eyes were embedded for semi-thin sectioning to analyse the acceptance angles (Methods, Spatial resolution and visual field). The two numbers are the mean minimum (17 ± 4 deg) and mean maximum (35 ± 9 deg) acceptance angle of the single ommatidia within the eye, so the range spans positions in the eye and is not a range between animals; ± not defined as SD or SE. The preceding Results sentence gives ommatidia 53 ± 12 um long and 16 ± 3 um wide.
where: Results, Spatial resolution and visual field of the compound eye
quote: They have a minimum acceptance angle of 17 ± 4° and a maximum acceptance angle of 35 ± 9°.
note: New-to-main value for this species and trait (acceptance_deg is a key already on main). Whole Results sentence (17 words); 'They' refers to the ommatidia named in the sentence before it ('The ommatidia themselves are 53 ± 12 μm long and 16 ± 3 μm wide.'), read in a second pass. Value is the two means in the sentence as a [minimum, maximum] pair. source.authors: Robert Sigl, Sebastian Steibl, Christian Laforsch
source.title: The role of vision for navigation in the crown-of-thorns seastar, Acanthaster planci

value: in field release trials, non-blinded adults found a reef structure significantly more often than blinded adults from 2.5 m and 5 m; no significant difference at 1.25 m or at 10 m
method: field release experiment at Temae beach: one blinded (terminal ossicle with optic cushion removed) and one non-blinded adult placed together at a start point downstream of a reef structure, 1.25, 2.5, 5 and 10 m away; success = reaching the structure; Fisher's exact test
conditions: Wild adults collected around Moorea, French Polynesia, and kept without food in plastic bins with running seawater for 2-4 weeks before use (Methods, Experimental animals and area). N = 10 trials per distance except 11 at 5 m (each trial one blinded and one non-blinded animal); one blinded animal at 2.5 m excluded after a pufferfish attack. Both groups moved with the prevailing current in a preliminary test and displacement did not differ (one-way ANOVA F1,8 = 0.052, p > 0.05; n = 5 trials). Nulls: at 1.25 m more non-blinded animals found the structure but the difference was not significant (p = 0.070); at 10 m eyesight did not significantly increase success (p = 0.105), although 30% of non-blinded animals still found it. Pooled across distances the vision effect was reported as p < 0.001. Blinded animals moved downstream at 2.5 m and beyond. The Methods do not describe randomisation of treatment or trial order. Field Nov-Dec 2013; tested animals had been kept unfed for 2-4 weeks.
where: Results, Field experiments, Experiment on visual navigation
quote: From a distance of 2.5 m and 5 m, non-blinded A. planci found the reef structure significantly more often than blinded A. planci (Fisher's exact test; p = 0.002 and p = 0.045, respectively).
note: Whole Results sentence (33 words), read intact in two abutting pieces ('From a distance of 2.5 m and 5 m, non-blinded A. planci found the reef structure significantly more often' | 'than blinded A. planci (Fisher's exact test; p = 0.002 and p = 0.045, respectively).'), final period seen. Value restates the quote and adds the two nulls (1.25 m, 10 m) from neighbouring Results sentences, which sit in conditions. Eyed-animal vision test filed under behaviour_vision per rules; vision effect assessed by eye ablation, not by a stimulus series. value: 76.9% of eyeless adults (eyestalks removed) responded to white light with tail-flipping, walking or swimming; all eyed adults responded

source.authors: Mary W. Donohue, Jonathan H. Cohen, Thomas W. Cronin
source.title: Cerebral photoreception in mantis shrimp

method: behavioural trial: animals dark-adapted for 1 h, then exposed for 2 min to white light from a food lamp (no wavelength or intensity given for the behavioural light); tail-flipping, walking or swimming scored from video; eyes removed at the eyestalk base at least 24 h before testing
conditions: Neogonodactylus oerstedii collected in the Florida Keys and held in laboratory aquaria on 12 h light:12 h dark. The paper gives no group sizes for eyed or eyeless animals, light or dark (not in the text, Methods or Figure 2 legend), so the percentages have no stated denominator. Dark controls of equal duration: the next Results sentence gives 25.0% (eyed) and 27.3% (eyeless) showing any of these behaviours in the dark, and says the light values were significantly greater than both; the test used is not given in that sentence. Response latency was longer for eyeless animals (6.7 s eyed vs 26.5 s eyeless; Mann-Whitney U, P<0.05). Cerebral photoreceptors recorded electrically (n = 2-5 flashes per preparation, three preparations) responded within 31 ms (±12 ms sd) of a 500 ms white xenon flash. Eyeless animals are a surgical preparation, not a natural state; the eyed value is 'all' with no n stated.
where: Results, Evidence for functional extraocular photoreceptors
quote: All eyed mantis shrimp showed one or more of these responses, whereas 76.9% of eyeless mantis shrimp responded according to our criteria (Fig. 2).
note: Whole Results sentence (25 words) read intact in two abutting pieces ('All eyed mantis shrimp showed one or more of these responses,' | 'whereas 76.9% of eyeless mantis shrimp responded according to our criteria (Fig. 2).'), final period seen; trailing figure reference kept inside the quote. 'These responses' = tail-flipping, walking, swimming as defined in Methods. Trait sense_light_nonvisual used for light detection by non-ocular photoreceptors in an animal (key exists on main). Family and order left blank as on main's gaps/try-species.json (family '' for this species); I could not open OBIS/WoRMS to take them.
